thread: Cardiff Castle furniture / movable property (became FOI 2026-020)
subject: FOI 2026-020 - Great House Farm, Llandough | Cardiff Castle Furniture
body:
Dear Sion

Thank you for your request for information received on 2nd July 2026, concerning furniture, furnishings, antiques, fixtures, heirlooms and other movable property originating from Great House Farm (Ty Mawr), Llandough.

Following searches of the Museum's collections management systems and associated records, Amgueddfa Cymru has not identified any furniture, furnishings, antiques, fixtures, heirlooms or other movable property recorded as originating from Great House Farm (Ty Mawr), Llandough.

Accordingly, Amgueddfa Cymru does not hold recorded information falling within the scope of items 1 to 9 of your request relating to such objects.
For clarity:

- We have not identified any objects of the type described in your request as originating from Great House Farm.
- We have not identified inventories, catalogues, acquisition records, disposal records, loan records, provenance files, ownership records, photographs, correspondence, reports, memoranda or related records concerning such objects within the scope of your request.
- We have not identified any records relating to the identification, recovery, ownership or location of furniture or household effects from Great House Farm.

We note your references to archaeological material from land associated with Great House Farm. However, archaeological finds are outside the scope of this response because they do not fall within your request for furniture, furnishings, antiques, fixtures, heirlooms and other movable property. We understand that archaeological material is the subject of a separate information request and will be dealt with separately.

Under section 1(1)(a) of the Freedom of Information Act 2000, our response is therefore that Amgueddfa Cymru does not hold the requested information.

Cofion cynnes,

FOI Team
Amgueddfa Cymru

thread: Cardiff Castle furniture / movable property (became FOI 2026-020)
subject: Re: FOI 2026-020 - Great House Farm, Llandough | Cardiff Castle Furniture
body:
Dear FOI Team,

Thank you for your response.

I note your position that Amgueddfa Cymru does not hold recorded information within the scope of my request.

However, I would be grateful if you could clarify the searches undertaken to reach that conclusion.

In particular, please confirm:

- Which collections management systems, databases and "associated records" were searched.
- Whether searches extended beyond accessioned objects to include acquisition files, provenance files, curator correspondence, donor files, temporary custody records, unaccessioned material, photographs and administrative records.
- The search terms used (for example: "Great House Farm", "Ty Mawr", "Llandough", "Williams", "Buckler", "Bute Estate" and any other relevant variants).
- Whether any potentially relevant records have been transferred to another institution or destroyed in accordance with a retention policy.

My original request was not limited to identifying surviving objects. It also sought records relating to their provenance, acquisition, transfer, ownership, photographs and correspondence. This reflects the fact that the contents of Great House Farm may have been dispersed following the property's demolition, meaning relevant records could exist even if no objects were ultimately accessioned by the Museum.

If, following those searches, Amgueddfa Cymru remains satisfied that no recorded information is held, I would be grateful for confirmation of that position.

Finally, if you are aware of another public authority that is more likely to hold records falling within the scope of my request, I would appreciate your advice in accordance with your duty to provide advice and assistance.

Thank you for your assistance.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler

thread: Cardiff Castle furniture / movable property (became FOI 2026-020)
subject: RE: FOI 2026-020 - Great House Farm, Llandough | Cardiff Castle Furniture
body:
Dear Sion

Thank you for your email.

Following receipt of your query, Amgueddfa Cymru undertook further enquiries to satisfy itself that no information had been overlooked when responding to your request.

These enquiries included a review of records held across the Museum's collections and a review of archived electronic systems and records by the Museum's Information Technology team. The review considered all collections management systems used by the Museum, including those most likely to contain information falling within the scope of your request.

For the History collections, searches were undertaken of the Collections Management System (CMS), accession files, donor indexes, location indexes and associated collection documentation. Searches were carried out using terms including "Great House Farm", "Ty Mawr", "Llandough", "Buckler" and "Bute". Additional consideration was given to acquisition records, provenance information and associated administrative records.

For the Art collections, searches were undertaken within the collections management system across description, comments, acquisition notes and place fields using the terms "Ty Mawr", "Great House Farm", "Great House", "Williams", "Buckler", "Llandough" and combinations of those terms. No additional paper archives relating to Great House Farm, Ty Mawr, Great House or Buckler were identified.

The Museum's Information Technology team also reviewed archived electronic systems and records retained by the Museum.

These enquiries identified some information relating generally to Great House Farm and the surrounding area. However, no information was identified concerning furniture, furnishings, antiques, fixtures, heirlooms or other movable property originating from Great House Farm (Ty Mawr), Llandough. We did not identify any inventories, catalogues, acquisition records, disposal records, loan records, provenance files, ownership records, photographs, correspondence or other records falling within categories 1 to 9 of your request.

We are also not aware of any relevant collection records relating to such material having been transferred to another institution or destroyed.

Accordingly, having completed these additional enquiries, Amgueddfa Cymru remains satisfied that it does not hold recorded information within the scope of your request and our response under section 1(1)(a) of the Freedom of Information Act 2000 remains unchanged.
In relation to your request for advice and assistance, Cardiff Council and Cardiff Castle would appear to be the organisations most likely to hold records relating to furniture, furnishings or other movable property associated with Great House Farm.

If you remain dissatisfied with this response, you may request an internal review within 40 working days of the date of this email.

Cofion cynnes,

FOI Team
Amgueddfa Cymru

thread: Cardiff Castle furniture / movable property (became FOI 2026-020)
subject: Re: FOI 2026-020 - Great House Farm, Llandough | Cardiff Castle Furniture — internal review request
body:
FOI Team,

Thank you for your detailed response and for undertaking the additional enquiries.

I appreciate the further information you have provided concerning the searches undertaken. However, I would like to request an internal review under the Freedom of Information Act 2000.

My concern is not simply that no objects have been identified. It is whether the searches undertaken have fully addressed the scope of my original request, particularly the documentary evidence concerning the provenance, acquisition, transfer, ownership, identification and dispersal of material originating from Great House Farm (Ty Mawr).

I would be grateful if the internal review could consider the following points.

1. Information identified concerning Great House Farm

Your response states that the additional enquiries identified "some information relating generally to Great House Farm and the surrounding area".

Please could you identify what categories of information this refers to and, where it is not exempt, provide the relevant recorded information or explain where it can be accessed?

This appears potentially relevant to the original request even if it does not itself identify furniture or household objects.

2. Scope of the archived electronic search

You state that the Information Technology team reviewed "archived electronic systems and records retained by the Museum".

Please could the review clarify:

- which archived systems were searched;
- the approximate date ranges covered;
- whether historical email or correspondence archives were searched;
- whether legacy collections-management databases were searched;
- whether databases or systems preceding the current CMS were searched; and
- whether any archived systems were unavailable, incomplete or incapable of being searched.

3. Correspondence and administrative records

My original request expressly sought correspondence concerning the identification, recovery, ownership or location of objects, as well as correspondence with the Bute Estate, Cardiff Council, Cardiff Castle and other public authorities.

Your response refers generally to "associated collection documentation" and "administrative records", but does not make clear whether historical correspondence files were specifically searched.

Please could the internal review establish whether searches were made of:

- curator correspondence;
- departmental correspondence files;
- donor correspondence;
- acquisition correspondence;
- disposal correspondence;
- loan correspondence;
- provenance correspondence;
- correspondence with Cardiff Council;
- correspondence with Cardiff Castle;
- correspondence with the Bute Estate;
- correspondence with other museums or public authorities; and
- any relevant institutional or external correspondence indexes.

4. Search terms

Thank you for identifying many of the search terms used.

Please could the internal review confirm whether the search also included combinations and variants involving: "Bute Estate", "Bute", "Cardiff Castle", "Cardiff Council", "Great House Farm", "Ty Mawr", "Great House", "Llandough", "Buckler", "Williams", "Mary Williams", "Mary Doreen Williams", "household effects", "contents", "furniture", "furnishings", "heirlooms", "fixtures", "estate", "dispersal", "recovery", "provenance", "ownership", "transfer", "demolition".

I appreciate that historical records may not have been consistently indexed, which is why I would be grateful for confirmation of the methodology used.

5. Transfer, disposal and destruction

Your response states:

"We are also not aware of any relevant collection records relating to such material having been transferred to another institution or destroyed."

Please could the internal review clarify whether this conclusion is based upon:

a. a search of transfer/accession-out records;
b. a review of retention and disposal records;
c. enquiries with relevant collections staff;
d. review of archival transfer documentation; or
e. institutional knowledge rather than a documentary search.

I am particularly interested in distinguishing between "no record exists" and "no record was identified in the systems searched".

6. The original request concerning external institutions

The original request was deliberately framed broadly because the question concerns possible dispersal of the contents of a demolished historic property.

It expressly included records concerning Cardiff Council, Cardiff Castle, the Bute Estate, museums, Arts Council England, DCMS, RCEWA and other public authorities.

I would therefore be grateful if the review could confirm whether records of communications or transactions involving those bodies were searched within Amgueddfa Cymru's records, rather than simply searching the Museum's object catalogue for Great House Farm objects.

7. Advice and assistance

You have stated that Cardiff Council and Cardiff Castle "would appear to be the organisations most likely to hold records relating to furniture, furnishings or other movable property associated with Great House Farm".

I appreciate that you cannot transfer another authority's records to me. However, could you please provide any further information available to the Museum as to which particular department, collection, archive or record series at Cardiff Council or Cardiff Castle is most likely to contain such material?

That would materially assist me in directing subsequent FOI and archival enquiries.

I am grateful for the additional work already undertaken. I am requesting the internal review because I would like the record to be clear as to precisely what was searched, what information was identified, and what the negative result does and does not establish.

I am not asking Amgueddfa Cymru to determine any allegation concerning the historical ownership of Great House Farm. The purpose of the review is simply to ensure that the documentary search corresponds fully with the scope of the original FOI request.

Please treat this email as my formal request for an internal review of FOI 2026-020.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber and Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member
Williams / Buckler Family Estate
